scope: Nested-output correction only. This is a code review, not a host publication receipt.
review:
**Verdict:** No blocking findings.

The nested no-tool hole is closed on the paths this patch actually owns. Known tool names reject as `noTool()`. Unknown part/delta types fail closed as `unknownOutput()`. Message `output_text`, reasoning/`summary_text`/`reasoning_text`, refusal, Google `text`/`thought`/`thought_signature`, and Anthropic `text_delta`/`thinking_delta`/`signature_delta`/`citations_delta` stay inert. Reasoning/thought/summary text is not copied into user text. Refusal on the Responses complete path now waits until every item and nested part is classified, so a refusal cannot mask a later tool or unknown part.

`scanResponseItem` returning `failure: classified` is a `WireDelta` (already `{ failure: ProviderFailure }` or equivalent). Callers return that object; they do not wrap it again.

## Limits (non-blocking)

- Unknown **top-level** stream event types still fall through to `return {}` in all three consumers. This patch classifies nested parts/deltas and (Responses) `output_item.done` / `content_part.*` only.
- Google `step.start` still classifies the step type only. Nested tool/unknown content on that event fails at `step.delta` or at `complete()`, not at start.
- Anthropic `complete()` still classifies sibling blocks only. That matches Messages shape; nested fail-closed for this dialect is the new delta classifier.
- `responseComplete` still returns cancelled/incomplete/failed before scanning `output`, so those terminals can still beat a nested tool/unknown part (pre-existing order).
- Inert catalogs are allow-lists. A legitimate new part name that is not in those sets will fail closed by design.

I did not run tests or open other files. Root’s before-fix reproduction and the focused 108 API tests are taken as given.
